```{r, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Detection and reaction can be separate. A hero entering an area might reveal a
door, play a sound, display an interaction prompt, or turn a tree into a monster.
`PhaserGame$add_proximity_trigger()` detects a distance transition; ordinary
browser or server actions decide what happens next.

This is **proximity**, not line of sight: it compares object centers and does
not check facing direction, artwork bounds, walls, or other obstructions.

## Try a one-time transformation

With the current package installed, run from the repository root:

```{r eval=FALSE}
shiny::runApp("inst/examples/proximity-transformation")
```

Move towards the tree with the arrow keys. Entering its 180-pixel radius hides
the tree and shows a prepared monster, entirely in the browser. Leaving and
returning does not repeat the reaction. Reload the app to reset it.

The complete example is:

```{r transformation-source, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
app_file <- system.file("examples", "proximity-transformation", "app.R",
                        package = "shinyphaser")
cat("```r\n", paste(readLines(app_file), collapse = "\n"), "\n```\n", sep = "")
```

`once = TRUE` fires only the first matching event. The tree and monster are
created ahead of time; the reaction changes visibility rather than dynamically
constructing a new actor. The monster stays in place. Pursuit and combat are
independent behaviours you can add afterwards.

## Choose a point or a moving target

Use `x` and `y` for a fixed point, as existing Swamps RPG doorway and key
triggers do:

```{r eval=FALSE}
game$add_proximity_trigger("door", "hero", x = 1450, y = 150,
  radius = 45, context = "mushroom_swamps", input_id = "near_door")
```

Use `target_name` instead of `x` and `y` to follow another scene object's
current position. Both the monitored object and target must exist and be
active. A hidden object can still be active: `hide()` changes visibility,
whereas map activation can also deactivate its body and scene activity.
A missing or inactive target is out of range. Objects that load asynchronously
are detected once they become available.

## React on entry and departure

The default `event = "both"` reports entering and leaving. Use `"enter"` or
`"leave"` for separate reactions. For example, after creating a guide and hint:

```{r eval=FALSE}
game$add_proximity_trigger("guide_enter", "hero", target_name = "guide",
  radius = 120, event = "enter",
  browser_action = browser_actions({hint$show()}))
game$add_proximity_trigger("guide_leave", "hero", target_name = "guide",
  radius = 120, event = "leave",
  browser_action = browser_actions({hint$hide()}))
```

These are edge events: staying within the radius does not repeatedly execute
the action. An object initially inside counts as an entry. An initial outside
state does not count as a departure. Leaving the configured map, or deactivating
an object, also ends proximity and can produce a leave event.

The optional `element_id` maintains an HTML element's visibility while near,
independently of `event` and `once`. If several triggers use the same element,
it remains visible while any of them is near.

## Run R logic when needed

Supply `input` and `server_action` for application state or Shiny UI updates:

```{r eval=FALSE}
game$add_proximity_trigger("guide", "hero", target_name = "guide",
  radius = 120, event = "enter", input = input,
  server_action = function(event) {
    shiny::showNotification("The guide is nearby.")
  })
```

The callback receives `id`, `active`, `event`, `objectName`, `targetName`, the
monitored object's `x` and `y`, and `targetX` and `targetY`. It uses a Shiny input
named `proximity_<id>` unless you specify `input_id`. Existing `input_id`
observers remain supported; no server input is sent when neither `input_id`
nor `server_action` is supplied. You may combine browser and server actions.

For a transformation that changes gameplay state, record that state in R as
well, and restore it when loading a game. `once` is browser-session trigger
state; it is not automatically persisted by `save_game()`.

## Replace or rearm a trigger

Calling `add_proximity_trigger()` with the same `id` replaces its configuration,
resets its detection and one-time state, and replaces its R callback. If the
object is already inside, re-registering can immediately produce an entry.
Use distinct IDs for separate enter and leave reactions.

The transformation demo has no tree collision body. If your tree has a separate
solid footprint, hiding its artwork does not remove that footprint. Update the
physics as part of the transformation too; for a map-based game, an R callback
can use `activate_map(..., hidden_objects = "tree_footprint")` to disable it.

## Where pursuit fits

`Sprite$set_movement()` provides generic following and wandering without any
built-in detection radius or alert. Proximity enter and leave actions choose
between those movement modes, and ordinary text actions display an alert.
Read [Make enemies approach using proximity](approach-on-sight.html) for the
complete composition and [Add close-range combat and life points](combat.html)
for a separate layer of combat rules.
